# Adjudication Task — Chapter 548

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃548화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“잘했다.”
  6|
  7|대회의실을 나서자마자 진위경이 건넨 말에, 나는 피식 웃는 것으로 대답을 대신했다.
  8|
  9|“왜 그러느냐?”
 10|
 11|“글쎄요. 말하는 내용과 다르게 표정이 좋지 않아서?”
 12|
 13|“아.”
 14|
 15|그제야 딱딱하게 굳어 있던 얼굴이 풀린다. 하지만 진위경의 입가에 맺힌 웃음은 금방 꺼질 듯이 흐릿했다.
 16|
 17|“사실 네 말을 어찌 받아들여야 할지 모르겠구나. 그만큼 오늘의 너는…….”
 18|
 19|“괜찮습니다. 사실 이런 반응이 당연한 거예요.”
 20|
 21|말꼬리를 흐리는 진위경을, 나는 이해했다. 그가 지금 어떤 심정인지 알 것 같았기 때문이다.
 22|
 23|‘같은 상황이었다면 나도 마찬가지였겠지.’
 24|
 25|이 세상에서 죽음이라는 단어는 생각만큼 무겁지 않다.
 26|
 27|현대의 살인 사건은 드물며 TV를 포함한 대중 매체로 알려지지만, 이곳에서는 빈번하게 목격되기 때문이다.
 28|
 29|치안이 좋은 도시라면 그나마 낫다. 그러나 그 밖의 양민들은 위치에 따라 산적이나 마적의 위협 속에서 살아가야 한다.
 30|
 31|무림인은 말할 것도 없다.
 32|
 33|‘칼끝을 걷는 삶.’
 34|
 35|오죽하면 도산검림(刀山劍林)이라 하겠나.
 36|
 37|그렇기에 그들은 늘 죽음을 각오한다. 투지를 불태우고 무공을 단련한다. 그리고 눈앞의 진위경 역시 한 사람의 무림인이었다.
 38|
 39|문제는, 그를 포함한 모두가 자라난 환경이다.
 40|
 41|무림에서는 죽이는 것도, 죽는 것도 사람이었다. 맹수와 영물(靈物)이 있었지만, 적어도 그것들의 정체는 듣도 보도 못한 괴물이 아니었다.
 42|
 43|하지만 오늘 나는…… 그 괴물들이 이 세상을 뒤덮을 것이라는 주장을 피력했다.
 44|
 45|사람과 괴물이 죽고 죽이는 싸움이 시작되리라 예견했다.
 46|
 47|‘내가 했던 말이 얼마나 와닿았는지는 모르겠지만, 그래도 위기감은 충분히 느꼈겠지.’
 48|
 49|내 이야기가 이어질수록 누군가는 불신 어린 시선을 보냈고 누군가는 혼란스러워하면서도 깊은 생각에 잠겼다.
 50|
 51|당장 모두가 믿지는 않더라도, 귀 기울여 들었다는 것만으로도 소기의 목적은 달성했다고 생각한다.
 52|
 53|‘그나마 상대가 무림인들이고, 확실한 물증이 있어서 이 정도라도 먹힌 거지.’
 54|
 55|늙은 선비들이 청중이었다면 공자후 아크바르를 외치며 괴력난신 반대 시위를 벌였겠지만, 대회의실에 모인 이들은 그렇게까지 앞뒤가 꽉 막힌 족속들이 아니었다.
 56|
 57|최소한 자신들의 눈앞에 팔 네 개 달린 괴물의 시체가 놓여 있는 상황에서는 그랬다.
 58|
 59|‘수신룡의 사체도 마찬가지고.’
 60|
 61|부위별로 분리 한 수신룡의 사체는 아직 극비리에 운송 중이다.
 62|
 63|하지만 내 인벤토리에는 만일을 대비하여 슬쩍 해 두었던 부산물 일부가 있었고, 그것은 중요한 물증이 되기에 충분했다.
 64|
 65|“그러고 보니 막내야. 그건 어디서 난 것이냐? 분명 빠지는 것 없이 챙긴 것으로 아는데.”
 66|
 67|“예?”
 68|
 69|“그 왜. 호북에서 쓰러트린 이무기의…….”
 70|
 71|“콜록, 콜록. 콜로로록!”
 72|
 73|억지로 쥐어 짜낸 기침을 토해 내자, 옆에서 대화를 듣고 있던 청풍이 품 안을 뒤적거렸다.
 74|
 75|“은인. 당과 드릴까요? 기침에는 당과가 최고예요.”
 76|
 77|“……싫어. 최악이야.”
 78|
 79|“네에.”
 80|
 81|도대체 언제부터 당과가 기적의 신약이 됐냐.
 82|
 83|단호한 실험 거부에 매드 사이언티스트 청풍이 시무룩한 얼굴로 당과를 제 입에 문다. 그 모습을 지켜보던 진위경이 피식 실소를 흘렸다.
 84|
 85|“알겠다. 더 묻지 않으마.”
 86|
 87|“음. 그럼 감사하고요.”
 88|
 89|머쓱하게 턱을 긁적이는 나를, 한동안 물끄러미 응시하던 진위경이 불쑥 입을 열었다.
 90|
 91|“문득 그런 생각이 들고는 한다. 네가, 우리 막내가 내가 알던 그 아이가 맞는지.”
 92|
 93|“……!”
 94|
 95|“구태여 묻지 않겠다. 더 이상의 의문도 품지 않으마. 다만 지금껏 네게 말하지 못한 한 가지 바람은 있다.”
 96|
 97|진위경의 부드러운 목소리가 이어졌다.
 98|
 99|“언젠가 이 모든 것이 마무리되고 적절한 때가 오면, 네가 미처 말하지 못한 이야기들을 듣고 싶구나.”
100|
101|말하지 못한 이야기라. 나는 마음속으로 뇌까렸다.
102|
103|‘언제쯤 그때가 올까.’
104|
105|하지만 정말 진위경의 말대로 이 모든 것들이 마무리된다면. 그리고 마음의 준비가 끝난다면…… 누구에게도 말할 수 없었던 나만의 비밀을 직접 말할지도 모르겠다.
106|
107|그런 날이 올지도 모르겠다.
108|
109|“……알겠습니다.”
110|
111|그리고 내가 씁쓸하게 웃으며 고개를 끄덕인, 바로 그 순간이었다.
112|
113|“여기 있었군. 화룡각주.”
114|
115|또각.
116|
117|늙수그레한 목소리와 함께 둔탁한 소음이 울려 퍼진다. 고개를 돌리자 그곳에는 무림맹 은영각주, 천면호리 송호가 있었다.
118|
119|“회의는 이미 한 식경 전에 끝났을 터인데. 아직도 여기에 남아 있다니. 우연인가?”
120|
121|그의 물음에 내가 고개를 저었다. 지금까지 무림맹에 남아 있던 것은, 비단 진위경과의 대화를 위해서만이 아니다.
122|
123|“필연일 겁니다.”
124|
125|“필연이라. 그래, 그렇군.”
126|
127|도무지 속을 짐작할 수 없는 노회한 눈동자에 묘한 빛이 스친다. 짧은 침묵 끝에 천면호리가 입을 열었다.
128|
129|“따라오게, 화룡각주. 무슨 일인지는 이미 알고 있겠지?”
130|
131|안다. 누가 나를 보고자 하는지도. 어떤 이유에서인지도.
132|
133|그리고 이어지는 천면호리의 한마디는 짐작을 확신으로 바꿔 주었다.
134|
135|“맹주께서 찾으시네.”
136|
137|
138|
139|* * *
140|
141|
142|
143|탁.
144|
145|등 뒤에서 문이 닫히는 소리가 유난히도 크게 울렸다. 맹주전 내부에 마련된 집무실에는 이미 두 사람이 나를 기다리고 있었다.
146|
147|“왔느냐?”
148|
149|덤덤한 적천강의 물음에 이어 무림 맹주 매종학이 손짓했다.
150|
151|“자리에 앉게. 그리고 자네들은 잠시 나가 있고.”
152|
153|나나, 내 뒤를 따라 곧장 집무실로 들어온 천면호리에게 하는 말이 아니다. 모습을 드러내지 않은 또 다른 이들에게 건네는 말이었다.
154|
155|스윽.
156|
157|매종학의 말이 끝나기 무섭게 유령처럼 사라지는 기척들.
158|
159|항상 그의 주위를 지킨다는 비밀 호위들마저 자리를 비키자, 나는 비어 있는 의자에 앉으며 입을 열었다.
160|
161|“수준이 엄청나네요. 기척이 거의 느껴지지 않던데요.”
162|
163|“이 방에 출입하는 대다수는 그마저도 모르지. 그걸 알아챈 자네가 대단한 거야.”
164|
165|“모르더라도 짐작은 하지 않을까요? 무림 맹주씩이나 되는 분께 호위 하나 없는 것도 이상하잖습니까.”
166|
167|“아. 그것도 그렇군.”
168|
169|또래의 청년처럼 턱을 긁적인 매종학이 문득 나를 바라본다. 맑고 깊은 눈동자에 내 얼굴이 비쳤다.
170|
171|“먼저, 자네가 대회의실에서 한 말들은 인상 깊게 들었네.”
172|
173|“그러셨다니 다행입니다. 다른 분들은 어떨지 모르겠네요.”
174|
175|“전부 믿지는 않더라도, 경시하지는 못할 걸세. 내 약속하지.”
176|
177|가볍게 건네는 말도 누구의 입에서 흘러나왔느냐에 따라 달라진다.
178|
179|그리고 그 대상이 무림맹의 맹주라면, 막강한 무게감이 실리는 것은 당연지사였다.
180|
181|‘내 주장에 한층 힘이 더해지겠군.’
182|
183|나쁘지 않은 흐름이다. 자연스럽게 내 얼굴이 살짝 풀리자 매종학이 빙긋 웃었다.
184|
185|“걱정했던 모양이군.”
186|
187|“아니라고 하면 거짓말이죠.”
188|
189|“말이 나왔으니 묻겠는데, 자네는 스스로의 주장을 얼마나 확신하고 있나?”
190|
191|“오 할. 반반입니다.”
192|
193|내 대답에 천면호리의 얼굴이 딱딱하게 굳었다.
194|
195|“지금…… 오 할이라고 했나?”
196|
197|“예. 생각하신 것보다 너무 적어서 그러십니까?”
198|
199|“빌어먹을. 그 반대지. 천하가 괴물로 뒤덮일 확률이 절반이나 된다는 소리 아닌가!”
200|
201|천면호리의 탄식에는 짧은 욕설이 포함되어 있었지만, 지금만큼은 아무도 신경 쓰지 않았다.
202|
203|나 역시 기분이 나쁘기는커녕 안도감이 들었다.
204|
205|반응을 보니 최소한 이 자리에 모인 이들만큼은 내 주장을 이미 기정사실로 받아들였다는 것을 알았기 때문이었다.
206|
207|“오 할이나 되는 근거는?”
208|
209|평정심을 잃지 않은 매종학의 물음에, 나는 망설임 없이 정해진 대답을 내놓았다.
210|
211|“제가 지금까지 암천을 상대하며 보고 느낀 전부입니다.”
212|
213|그때, 말없이 차 대신 독한 화주를 홀짝거리던 적천강이 불쑥 입을 열었다.
214|
215|“네놈의 판단이 틀렸을 수도 있다.”
216|
217|“평생 욕 오지게 먹어도 좋으니까, 제발 그랬으면 좋겠습니다.”
218|
219|진심이다. 차라리 내 예측이 완전히 빗나가서 사실 암천이 별것 아닌 놈들이고, 변이 몬스터 같은 놈들도 나타나지 않았으면 좋겠다.
220|
221|나 한 사람 욕먹는 정도로 해피엔딩을 볼 수 있다면 남는 장사니까.
222|
223|그러나…….
224|
225|“미친 얘기 같지만, 전부 사실이에요.”
226|
227|“염병할. 미치겠군.”
228|
229|“그 정도로 안 믿기십니까?”
230|
231|“믿기 싫다. 네 녀석이 하는 말이 아니었다면 그랬을 게다.”
232|
233|“……!”
234|
235|갑자기 치고 들어오는 감동 뭐야. 어쩔 거야, 이거.
236|
237|탁.
238|
239|그러나 감동이고 나발이고. 술병을 거칠게 내려놓은 적천강이 나를 노려보았다.
240|
241|“차라리 거짓말이라고 말해라. 지금이라도 이실직고한다면 화염신장 세 대 정도로 끝내줄 테니.”
242|
243|“이 자리에서 제 불알을 걸고 맹세컨대. 그냥 하는 소리가 아닙니다. 그리고 화염신장 세 대 맞으면 저 죽어요.”
244|
245|“후우.”
246|
247|깊은 한숨을 내쉰 적천강이 매종학과 천면호리를 향해 입술을 뗐다.
248|
249|“노부도 믿기 싫지만…… 저놈이 하는 말이 전부 사실인 모양이오. 최소한 자기 불알을 걸 때만큼은 진심이거든.”
250|
251|“…….”
252|
253|진위 여부를 정하는 기준이 좀 이상하긴 한데, 어쨌든 내 진심이 제대로 전해지긴 한 모양이다.
254|
255|그리고 우려가 현실로 나타남과 동시에 집무실에 내려앉은 침묵은, 잠시 후 들려온 매종학의 한 마디에 의해 깨져 나갔다.
256|
257|“한 가지만 더 묻겠네.”
258|
259|“두 개 물어보셔도 되는데요.”
260|
261|“아니, 하나면 충분해.”
262|
263|스윽.
264|
265|매종학이 말과 함께 손가락을 까딱였다.
266|
267|동시에 그의 등 뒤, 가득 쌓여 있는 죽간들 사이에서 커다란 두루마리가 날아와 우리가 앉아 있는 탁자 위로 펼쳐졌다.
268|
269|촤르륵.
270|
271|두루마리에 적혀 있는, 아니 그려져 있는 것을 확인한 내가 중얼거렸다.
272|
273|“이건…….”
274|
275|“보는 그대로일세. 천하의 전도(全圖)지.”
276|
277|매종학의 말처럼 그건 천하 곳곳의 지리와 지형, 거기에 더해 지명을 표기한 지도였다.
278|
279|하지만 내가 지금껏 무림에서 봤던 어느 지도보다도 크고, 특별한 차이가 있었다.
280|
281|“각 문파의 위치까지 표시되어 있군요.”
282|
283|“무림맹을 위해 만들어진 것이니까. 그럼 묻건대…….”
284|
285|매종학의 덤덤한 목소리가 귓가를 파고들었다.
286|
287|“자네는, 암천의 다음 목표가 어디라고 생각하나?”
288|
289|“확신할 수 없습니다.”
290|

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

*It only got through at all because they’re martial artists and I had hard evidence.*

[P27]
If my audience had been a bunch of old Confucian scholars, they would have shouted “Confucius Akbar!” and staged a protest against supernatural powers. The people in the great conference hall were not quite that close-minded.

[P28]
At least, not with the corpse of a four-armed monster lying in front of them.

[P29]
*There were the Water God Dragon’s remains, too.*

[P30]
Its body had been separated into parts and was still being transported in strict secrecy. But I had quietly slipped some of its byproducts into my Inventory just in case. Those were enough to serve as important physical evidence.

[P31]
“Come to think of it, Youngest. Where did you get that? I was sure every last piece had been collected.”

[P32]
“What?”

[P33]
“You know. The imugi you defeated in Hubei…”

[P34]
“Ahem. Ahem. Cough-cough-cough!”

[P35]
I forced out a fit of coughing. Cheongpung, who had been listening beside us, rummaged through his robes.

[P36]
“Benefactor. Would you like a sweetmeat? Sweetmeats are the best thing for a cough.”

[P37]
“…No. They’re the worst.”

[P38]
“Okay.”

[P39]
*Since when were sweetmeats miracle medicine?*

[P40]
Denied a test subject, mad scientist Cheongpung looked dejected and put a sweetmeat in his own mouth. Jin Wikyung watched him and let out a quiet laugh.

[P41]
“I understand. I won’t ask again.”

[P42]
“Good. Thanks.”

[P43]
I scratched my chin awkwardly. Jin Wikyung watched me for a long moment, then spoke.

[P44]
“Sometimes I wonder whether you—our youngest—are the same child I knew.”

[P45]
“……!”

[P46]
“I won’t press you. I won’t let myself doubt you any further, either. But there is one thing I’ve wanted to ask of you, though I’ve never said it.”

[P47]
His voice remained gentle.

[P48]
“When all this is over, and the time is right, I’d like to hear the stories you haven’t been able to tell me.”

[P49]
*The stories I haven’t been able to tell.*

[P50]
I repeated the words to myself.

[P51]
*When will that time come?*

[P52]
But if all this really did end, as Jin Wikyung said, and I was ready… maybe I would tell him myself. The secret I had never been able to share with anyone.

[P53]
Maybe that day would come.

[P54]
“…I understand.”

[P55]
I gave him a bitter smile and nodded. At that exact moment, a voice called out.

[P56]
“There you are, Fire Dragon Pavilion Master.”

[P57]
*Tap.*

[P58]
An elderly voice, followed by a heavy footfall. I turned to see Song Ho, the Thousand-Faced Fox and Chief of the Murim Alliance’s Hidden Shadow Pavilion.

[P59]
“The meeting ended half an hour ago, yet you’re still here. Coincidence?”

[P60]
I shook my head. Talking to Jin Wikyung was not the only reason I had stayed at the Murim Alliance.

[P61]
“I don’t think so.”

[P62]
“No. Neither do I.”

[P63]
Something flickered in those old, unreadable eyes. After a brief silence, the Thousand-Faced Fox spoke again.

[P64]
“Come with me, Fire Dragon Pavilion Master. You know what this is about, don’t you?”

[P65]
I did. I knew who wanted to see me, and why.

[P66]
His next words turned my guess into certainty.

[P67]
“The Alliance Leader is looking for you.”

[P68]
* * *

[P69]
*Thud.*

[P70]
The door closed behind me with an unusually loud sound. Two people were already waiting in an office inside the Alliance Leader’s Hall.

[P71]
“You’re here?”

[P72]
After Jeok Cheongang’s flat question, Murim Alliance Leader Mae Jonghak gestured toward a seat.

[P73]
“Sit down. The rest of you, wait outside for a moment.”

[P74]
He was not speaking to me or the Thousand-Faced Fox, who had followed me straight into the office. He meant the others who had yet to show themselves.

[P75]
*Swish.*

[P76]
No sooner had Mae Jonghak spoken than several presences vanished like ghosts.

[P77]
Even the secret guards said to remain at his side at all times had withdrawn. I sat in an empty chair.

[P78]
“They’re incredibly skilled. I could barely sense them.”

[P79]
“Most people who enter this room don’t notice them at all. It’s impressive that you did.”

[P80]
“Even if they don’t notice, wouldn’t they guess? It would be strange for the Murim Alliance Leader to have no guards.”

[P81]
“Ah. You have a point.”

[P82]
Mae Jonghak scratched his chin like a young man my age, then looked at me. My face was reflected in his clear, deep eyes.

[P83]
“First, I was impressed by what you said in the great conference hall.”

[P84]
“I’m glad to hear it. I don’t know what the others thought.”

[P85]
“They may not believe all of it, but they won’t dismiss it. I promise you.”

[P86]
Even a casually spoken promise carried weight when it came from the right person. Coming from the Murim Alliance Leader, it carried a great deal.

[P87]
*That gives my argument more weight.*

[P88]
Things were going well. My expression must have relaxed, because Mae Jonghak smiled.

[P89]
“You were worried.”

[P90]
“I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t.”

[P91]
“Since we’re on the subject, how certain are you of your claim?”

[P92]
“Five out of ten. Fifty-fifty.”

[P93]
The Thousand-Faced Fox’s face went rigid.

[P94]
“Did you just say… five out of ten?”

[P95]
“Yes. Is that lower than you expected?”

[P96]
“Damn it, the opposite! You’re saying there’s a fifty-percent chance the world will be covered in monsters!”

[P97]
There was a curse in his outburst, but no one cared about that now. Far from taking offense, I felt relieved.

[P98]
Judging by his reaction, at least the people in this room had already accepted my claim as something they had to reckon with.

[P99]
“What gives you that fifty percent?”

[P100]
Mae Jonghak was still calm. I answered without hesitation.

[P101]
“Everything I’ve seen and felt fighting Dark Heaven.”

[P102]
Jeok Cheongang, who had been sipping strong liquor instead of tea, spoke up.

[P103]
“You could be wrong.”

[P104]
“I hope I am. They can curse me for the rest of my life if I am.”

[P105]
I meant it. I would much rather be completely wrong. Maybe Dark Heaven would turn out to be nothing special, and no monsters like that mutant would ever appear.

[P106]
If all it took to get a happy ending was for everyone to curse me, I’d take that deal.

[P107]
But…

[P108]
“It sounds insane, but it’s all true.”

[P109]
“Damn it. This is driving me crazy.”

[P110]
“Is it that hard to believe?”

[P111]
“I don’t want to believe it. If it were anyone but you saying it, I wouldn’t.”

[P112]
“……!”

[P113]
*Where did that come from? What am I supposed to do with that?*

[P114]
*Thud.*

[P115]
But to hell with being moved. Jeok Cheongang slammed his liquor bottle down and glared at me.

[P116]
“Tell me it’s a lie. Confess now, and I’ll let you off with three strikes from the Flame Divine Palm.”

[P117]
“I swear on my balls, right here and now, that I’m not making this up. Also, three strikes from the Flame Divine Palm would kill me.”

[P118]
“Haa.”

[P119]
Jeok Cheongang let out a deep sigh and turned to Mae Jonghak and the Thousand-Faced Fox.

[P120]
“This old man doesn’t want to believe it either, but it seems the punk is telling the truth. He’s sincere when he puts his balls on the line, at least.”

[P121]
“……”

[P122]
That was a strange standard for deciding whether something was true. Still, I seemed to have gotten my sincerity across.

[P123]
As what I feared settled over the office, silence fell. Mae Jonghak broke it.

[P124]
“I have one more question.”

[P125]
“You can ask two.”

[P126]
“No. One is enough.”

[P127]
*Swish.*

[P128]
Mae Jonghak crooked a finger. A large scroll flew out from among the bamboo slips piled behind him and unfurled across our table.

[P129]
*Rustle.*

[P130]
I looked at what was written on it—no, drawn—and muttered, “This is…”

[P131]
“A complete map of the realm.”

[P132]
It showed the geography and terrain across the realm, with place names marked as well. But it was larger than any map I had seen in Murim, and there was another difference.

[P133]
“It even shows where the sects are.”

[P134]
“It was made for the Murim Alliance. Now, tell me…”

[P135]
Mae Jonghak’s calm voice reached my ears.

[P136]
“Where do you think Dark Heaven will strike next?”

[P137]
“I can’t be certain.”

[P138]
“Who can be certain of the future? A guess will do.”

[P139]
*A guess…*

[P140]
I thought in silence for a while. Then I raised my hand and touched one part of the map.

[P141]
*Tap.*

[P142]
“Here.”

[P143]
The reaction was immediate.

[P144]
Jeok Cheongang muttered a curse. A sharp light flashed in the Thousand-Faced Fox’s eyes, and Mae Jonghak leaned toward me.

[P145]
“Why there?”

[P146]
“If what happened in Hubei happens again, Dark Heaven would have a hard time finding a better place.”

[P147]
“You mean that ‘rift.’”

[P148]
“Yes.”

[P149]
“You’re certain the rift will open again—or rather, you suspect it will?”

[P150]
“I think there’s every chance it will. What happened wasn’t a natural disaster. Dark Heaven planned it and made it happen.”

[P151]
*There can only be a first if there’s a second.*

[P152]
I alone had been able to glimpse the Water God Dragon’s memories, however briefly. I had no physical evidence I could offer with confidence, and I could not be certain. But there was a good chance Dark Heaven had its sights on *that place*.

[P153]
I continued calmly.

[P154]
“I don’t know what Dark Heaven will do next. This might not be its immediate target. But at least one person must already be on her way there.”

[P155]
“The Southern Heaven Demon Empress.”

[P156]
At the sound of the title, the countless bodies I had seen in Hubei flashed before my eyes. My fist clenched.

[P157]
“That’s right. The Southern Heaven Demon Empress… she must have that place in mind.”

[P158]
“Another guess?”

[P159]
“A guess. One close to certainty.”

[P160]
I could not be sure of anything. But a thought that had been haunting me for some time seemed more and more likely.

[P161]
Mae Jonghak nodded quietly and looked to Song Ho.

[P162]
“What do you think, Chief of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion?”

[P163]
“I’ll add my voice to the Fire Dragon Pavilion Master’s.”

[P164]
Song Ho answered at once, then continued.

[P165]
“It has been more than seven days and nights since we sent a missive. With no reply yet, there’s a good chance something has already gone wrong.”

[P166]
“I expected as much, but… that’s fast.”

[P167]
“Yes. We could send the Outer Hall forces we selected in advance, but we risk arriving too late.”

[P168]
*A missive? Forces selected in advance?*

[P169]
The Thousand-Faced Fox read the question on my face.

[P170]
“The Hidden Shadow Pavilion has eyes and ears throughout the realm. You weren’t the only one to make this guess.”

[P171]
“…You were already watching that place.”

[P172]
“Since immediately after we received the report on what happened in Hubei Province, to be precise. But neither I nor anyone else in the Pavilion anticipated that strange phenomenon you call a rift.”

[P173]
I remembered something I had briefly forgotten. The elderly martial artist before me had been the head of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion forty years ago, and he still was.

[P174]
And there was only one person in this room who could give orders to both of us.

[P175]
“Fire Dragon Pavilion Master Jin Taekyung.”

[P176]
Mae Jonghak’s voice rang through the office, heavier than usual.

[P177]
The great martial artist known as the Number One Sword Under Heaven, the man now standing at the pinnacle of Murim, fixed his clear blue eyes on me.

[P178]
“I’m giving you your first order.”

[P179]
* * *

[P180]
*Whoosh!*

[P181]
A fierce wind rose with every step I took.

[P182]
I paid no mind to who saw me use my movement technique. I rushed back to my residence and threw the door open.

[P183]
*Bang!*

[P184]
A familiar face came into view.

[P185]
Hyuk Mujin sprang up from where he had been lounging in the annex. He looked from me to the shattered door and muttered, “Welcome ba—wow. The owner’s going to cry tears of blood. That door was replaced less than half an hour ago.”

[P186]
I had no time to sympathize with the owner. Instead of greeting Mujin, I gave him an order.

[P187]
“Summon everyone.”

[P188]
“What?”

[P189]
He stared at me, dumbfounded.

[P190]
“What’s that supposed to mean all of a sudden? Wait—summon who?”

[P191]
“The Fire Dragon Pavilion.”

[P192]
“What?”

[P193]
“We have a mission. Right now.”

[P194]
“Wait. Hold on! Captain, why all of a sudden? Where are we going?”

[P195]
I answered his wide-eyed stare in a low voice.

[P196]
“Nanman.”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.

*The stories I haven’t been able to tell.*

[P50]
I repeated the words to myself.

[P51]
*When will that time come?*

[P52]
But if all this really did end, as Jin Wikyung said, and I was ready… maybe I would tell him myself. The secret I had never been able to share with anyone.

[P53]
Maybe that day would come.

[P54]
“…I understand.”

[P55]
I gave him a bitter smile and nodded. At that exact moment, a voice called out.

[P56]
“There you are, Fire Dragon Pavilion Master.”

[P57]
*Tap.*

[P58]
An elderly voice, followed by a heavy footfall. I turned to see Song Ho, the Thousand-Faced Fox and Chief of the Murim Alliance’s Hidden Shadow Pavilion.

[P59]
“The meeting ended half an hour ago, yet you’re still here. Coincidence?”

[P60]
I shook my head. Talking to Jin Wikyung was not the only reason I had stayed at the Murim Alliance.

[P61]
“I don’t think so.”

[P62]
“No. Neither do I.”

[P63]
Something flickered in those old, unreadable eyes. After a brief silence, the Thousand-Faced Fox spoke again.

[P64]
“Come with me, Fire Dragon Pavilion Master. You know what this is about, don’t you?”

[P65]
I did. I knew who wanted to see me, and why.

[P66]
His next words turned my guess into certainty.

[P67]
“The Alliance Leader is looking for you.”

[P68]
* * *

[P69]
*Thud.*

[P70]
The door closed behind me with an unusually loud sound. Two people were already waiting in an office inside the Alliance Leader’s Hall.

[P71]
“You’re here?”

[P72]
After Jeok Cheongang’s flat question, Murim Alliance Leader Mae Jonghak gestured toward a seat.

[P73]
“Sit down. The rest of you, wait outside for a moment.”

[P74]
He was not speaking to me or the Thousand-Faced Fox, who had followed me straight into the office. He meant the others who had yet to show themselves.

[P75]
*Swish.*

[P76]
No sooner had Mae Jonghak spoken than several presences vanished like ghosts.

[P77]
Even the secret guards said to remain at his side at all times had withdrawn. I sat in an empty chair.

[P78]
“They’re incredibly skilled. I could barely sense them.”

[P79]
“Most people who enter this room don’t notice them at all. It’s impressive that you did.”

[P80]
“Even if they don’t notice, wouldn’t they guess? It would be strange for the Murim Alliance Leader to have no guards.”

[P81]
“Ah. You have a point.”

[P82]
Mae Jonghak scratched his chin like a young man my age, then looked at me. My face was reflected in his clear, deep eyes.

[P83]
“First, I was impressed by what you said in the great conference hall.”

[P84]
“I’m glad to hear it. I don’t know what the others thought.”

[P85]
“They may not believe all of it, but they won’t dismiss it. I promise you.”

[P86]
Even a casually spoken promise carried weight when it came from the right person. Coming from the Murim Alliance Leader, it carried a great deal.

[P87]
*That gives my argument more weight.*

[P88]
Things were going well. My expression must have relaxed, because Mae Jonghak smiled.

[P89]
“You were worried.”

[P90]
“I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t.”

[P91]
“Since we’re on the subject, how certain are you of your claim?”

[P92]
“Five out of ten. Fifty-fifty.”

[P93]
The Thousand-Faced Fox’s face went rigid.

[P94]
“Did you just say… five out of ten?”

[P95]
“Yes. Is that lower than you expected?”

[P96]
“Damn it, the opposite! You’re saying there’s a fifty-percent chance the world will be covered in monsters!”

[P97]
There was a curse in his outburst, but no one cared about that now. Far from taking offense, I felt relieved.

[P98]
Judging by his reaction, at least the people in this room had already accepted my claim as something they had to reckon with.

[P99]
“What gives you that fifty percent?”

[P100]
Mae Jonghak was still calm. I answered without hesitation.

[P101]
“Everything I’ve seen and felt fighting Dark Heaven.”

[P102]
Jeok Cheongang, who had been sipping strong liquor instead of tea, spoke up.

[P103]
“You could be wrong.”

[P104]
“I hope I am. They can curse me for the rest of my life if I am.”

[P105]
I meant it. I would much rather be completely wrong. Maybe Dark Heaven would turn out to be nothing special, and no monsters like that mutant would ever appear.

[P106]
If all it took to get a happy ending was for everyone to curse me, I’d take that deal.

[P107]
But…

[P108]
“It sounds insane, but it’s all true.”

[P109]
“Damn it. This is driving me crazy.”

[P110]
“Is it that hard to believe?”

[P111]
“I don’t want to believe it. If it were anyone but you saying it, I wouldn’t.”

[P112]
“……!”

[P113]
*Where did that come from? What am I supposed to do with that?*

[P114]
*Thud.*

[P115]
But to hell with being moved. Jeok Cheongang slammed his liquor bottle down and glared at me.

[P116]
“Tell me it’s a lie. Confess now, and I’ll let you off with three strikes from the Flame Divine Palm.”

[P117]
“I swear on my balls, right here and now, that I’m not making this up. Also, three strikes from the Flame Divine Palm would kill me.”

[P118]
“Haa.”

[P119]
Jeok Cheongang let out a deep sigh and turned to Mae Jonghak and the Thousand-Faced Fox.

[P120]
“This old man doesn’t want to believe it either, but it seems the punk is telling the truth. He’s sincere when he puts his balls on the line, at least.”

[P121]
“……”

[P122]
That was a strange standard for deciding whether something was true. Still, I seemed to have gotten my sincerity across.

[P123]
As what I feared settled over the office, silence fell. Mae Jonghak broke it.

[P124]
“I have one more question.”

[P125]
“You can ask two.”

[P126]
“No. One is enough.”

[P127]
*Swish.*

[P128]
Mae Jonghak crooked a finger. A large scroll flew out from among the bamboo slips piled behind him and unfurled across our table.

[P129]
*Rustle.*

[P130]
I looked at what was written on it—no, drawn—and muttered, “This is…”

[P131]
“A complete map of the realm.”

[P132]
It showed the geography and terrain across the realm, with place names marked as well. But it was larger than any map I had seen in Murim, and there was another difference.

[P133]
“It even shows where the sects are.”

[P134]
“It was made for the Murim Alliance. Now, tell me…”

[P135]
Mae Jonghak’s calm voice reached my ears.

[P136]
“Where do you think Dark Heaven will strike next?”

[P137]
“I can’t be certain.”

[P138]
“Who can be certain of the future? A guess will do.”

[P139]
*A guess…*

[P140]
I thought in silence for a while. Then I raised my hand and touched one part of the map.

[P141]
*Tap.*

[P142]
“Here.”

[P143]
The reaction was immediate.

[P144]
Jeok Cheongang muttered a curse. A sharp light flashed in the Thousand-Faced Fox’s eyes, and Mae Jonghak leaned toward me.

[P145]
“Why there?”

[P146]
“If what happened in Hubei happens again, Dark Heaven would have a hard time finding a better place.”

[P147]
“You mean that ‘rift.’”

[P148]
“Yes.”

[P149]
“You’re certain the rift will open again—or rather, you suspect it will?”

[P150]
“I think there’s every chance it will. What happened wasn’t a natural disaster. Dark Heaven planned it and made it happen.”

[P151]
*There can only be a first if there’s a second.*

[P152]
I alone had been able to glimpse the Water God Dragon’s memories, however briefly. I had no physical evidence I could offer with confidence, and I could not be certain. But there was a good chance Dark Heaven had its sights on *that place*.

[P153]
I continued calmly.

[P154]
“I don’t know what Dark Heaven will do next. This might not be its immediate target. But at least one person must already be on her way there.”

[P155]
“The Southern Heaven Demon Empress.”

[P156]
At the sound of the title, the countless bodies I had seen in Hubei flashed before my eyes. My fist clenched.

[P157]
“That’s right. The Southern Heaven Demon Empress… she must have that place in mind.”

[P158]
“Another guess?”

[P159]
“A guess. One close to certainty.”

[P160]
I could not be sure of anything. But a thought that had been haunting me for some time seemed more and more likely.

[P161]
Mae Jonghak nodded quietly and looked to Song Ho.

[P162]
“What do you think, Chief of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion?”

[P163]
“I’ll add my voice to the Fire Dragon Pavilion Master’s.”

[P164]
Song Ho answered at once, then continued.

[P165]
“It has been more than seven days and nights since we sent a missive. With no reply yet, there’s a good chance something has already gone wrong.”

[P166]
“I expected as much, but… that’s fast.”

[P167]
“Yes. We could send the Outer Hall forces we selected in advance, but we risk arriving too late.”

[P168]
*A missive? Forces selected in advance?*

[P169]
The Thousand-Faced Fox read the question on my face.

[P170]
“The Hidden Shadow Pavilion has eyes and ears throughout the realm. You weren’t the only one to make this guess.”

[P171]
“…You were already watching that place.”

[P172]
“Since immediately after we received the report on what happened in Hubei Province, to be precise. But neither I nor anyone else in the Pavilion anticipated that strange phenomenon you call a rift.”

[P173]
I remembered something I had briefly forgotten. The elderly martial artist before me had been the head of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion forty years ago, and he still was.

[P174]
And there was only one person in this room who could give orders to both of us.

[P175]
“Fire Dragon Pavilion Master Jin Taekyung.”

[P176]
Mae Jonghak’s voice rang through the office, heavier than usual.

[P177]
The great martial artist known as the Number One Sword Under Heaven, the man now standing at the pinnacle of Murim, fixed his clear blue eyes on me.

[P178]
“I’m giving you your first order.”

[P179]
* * *

[P180]
*Whoosh!*

[P181]
A fierce wind rose with every step I took.

[P182]
I paid no mind to who saw me use my movement technique. I rushed back to my residence and threw the door open.

[P183]
*Bang!*

[P184]
A familiar face came into view.

[P185]
Hyuk Mujin sprang up from where he had been lounging in the annex. He looked from me to the shattered door and muttered, “Welcome ba—wow. The owner’s going to cry tears of blood. That door was replaced less than half an hour ago.”

[P186]
I had no time to sympathize with the owner. Instead of greeting Mujin, I gave him an order.

[P187]
“Summon everyone.”

[P188]
“What?”

[P189]
He stared at me, dumbfounded.

[P190]
“What’s that supposed to mean all of a sudden? Wait—summon who?”

[P191]
“The Fire Dragon Pavilion.”

[P192]
“What?”

[P193]
“We have a mission. Right now.”

[P194]
“Wait. Hold on! Captain, why all of a sudden? Where are we going?”

[P195]
I answered his wide-eyed stare in a low voice.

[P196]
“Nanman.”

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.

- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style
